references.title: Best fitness tracker 2026: Top picks from Apple, Fitbit, Garmin and more
The best fitness trackers 2026: From Fitbit-style bands to smartwatches and screen-free trackers
Best Fitness Trackers 2026, Trainer Tested
I tested the Fitbit Air for a week and it's the best no-fuss fitness tracker in 2026
WHOOP Pricing 2026: All 3 Plans Compared ($199-$359/yr)
Xiaomi Smart Band 10 review
Best fitness tracker 2026: Reviewed, tested, and compared
Xiaomi 手環 10 台灣官方售價
Garmin announces the Venu 4 with new health & fitness features
Oura unveils its Ring 5 with a thinner, lighter design starting at $399

en.commentary:
The fitness tracker market split into two business models in 2026, and that split now decides more purchases than any sensor spec does. On one side sit devices you buy once. On the other sit devices whose price keeps arriving every month. I built this ranking around three-year total cost for exactly that reason, and the order changes noticeably once the membership fees are written into the price.

Garmin Venu 4 takes the top spot. Its health status monitor learns where your own heart rate, HRV and skin temperature normally sit, then flags the moment one of them drifts away, and this is the first tracker at this price to key its alerts to you rather than to a population average. Lifestyle logging closes the loop by connecting last night's caffeine and alcohol to that night's sleep score. It runs 12 days per charge, Garmin Connect keeps every metric outside the paywall, and at $499.99 the three-year cost is still $499.99.

Garmin Venu 3 holds second and stays the smarter buy at $449.99 for most readers. It matches the Venu 4 on day-to-day step, heart rate and sleep staging accuracy, runs 14 days per charge, and includes Body Battery and Sleep Coach for the life of the hardware. The extra $50 buys the health status layer and the lifestyle logging, so pay it only if you will actually read those screens.

Fitbit Charge 6 is the one I recommend to most people at $159.95. Its sleep trend reporting is the easiest to act on that I have used, and it carries ECG heart rhythm assessment plus EDA stress sensing in a band you forget you are wearing.

Fitbit Air is the product of the year in this category. Google shipped it on May 26, 2026 at $99.99: 12 grams, a fabric band and a small sensor pebble, all data flowing into the Google Health app with a Gemini coach layered on top. Core sleep, heart rate and step tracking stay free permanently. In two-week independent testing its total sleep landed within about 13 minutes of Oura Ring 4 and resting heart rate within about 3 bpm, and a 2026 JMIR Formative Research study found Fitbit's optical heart rate more accurate than Oura's during activity.

Oura Ring 5 shipped on June 4 at $399, 40 percent smaller than the Ring 4 and the smallest smart ring you can buy today. The sleep and readiness scoring that made the Ring 4 worth wearing carries over intact, and that size reduction is what moves it above the Ring 4 here.

Run the three-year math and the picture sharpens. Fitbit Air costs $99.99 over three years. WHOOP Peak at $239 a year reaches $717. Oura Ring 5 at $399 plus $5.99 a month reaches roughly $615. Both of those earn their keep for a specific reader, and I say who below.

highlights.title: Garmin Venu 4 wins because its alerts are keyed to your own baseline
highlights.body: Health status monitoring is the feature that moved the Venu 4 past the Venu 3 for me. It learns where your resting heart rate, HRV and skin temperature normally sit and raises a flag when one of them starts moving, which catches the run-down day before you feel it. Lifestyle logging then shows what the caffeine and the wine did to that night's sleep, so the alert arrives with a cause attached. Twelve days of battery keeps it on your wrist overnight, where the sleep data actually comes from, and every one of these metrics is included in the $499.99 with nothing left to renew.

highlights.title: Fitbit Air at $99.99 is the most important launch this category has seen in years
highlights.body: Google removed the screen, dropped the weight to 12 grams and priced the whole thing at $99.99 with permanent free access to sleep, heart rate, steps, SpO2 and skin temperature. The accuracy holds: two weeks of side-by-side testing put its total sleep within roughly 13 minutes of Oura Ring 4 and resting heart rate within about 3 bpm, and the 2026 JMIR Formative Research work gives Fitbit the edge on optical heart rate during exercise. Buying it once and owning the data forever is the strongest value proposition on this list.

highlights.title: Count the subscription before you compare anything else
highlights.body: Three-year totals reorder this entire market. Fitbit Air: $99.99. Fitbit Charge 6: $159.95. Garmin Venu 3: $449.99. Oura Ring 4: about $565 once you add $5.99 a month to the $349 ring. WHOOP Peak: $717 at $239 a year, with the membership carrying the hardware and the PowerPack charger. Those last two make sense for readers who want continuous recovery modelling as an ongoing service. For anyone who wants to buy a device and be done, the buy-once column is where I would shop.

highlights.title: Accuracy splits by axis, and the expensive device wins only on its own axis
highlights.body: The useful finding from 2026 testing is that these devices separate by what they measure best. Oura Ring 4 leads on sleep staging and overnight HRV with the smallest total-sleep bias in the group at about three minutes. WHOOP 5.0 leads on continuous strain and recovery through hard training blocks. Fitbit takes optical heart rate during activity. Garmin takes all-round consistency across steps, workouts and sleep. Pick the axis that matches your training and the price question mostly answers itself.

highlights.title: Under $100, Xiaomi Smart Band 10 and Amazfit Band 7 deliver far more than the price suggests
highlights.body: Xiaomi Smart Band 10 sells for around $51 with a bigger 1.72-inch AMOLED panel this generation, accurate step and heart rate tracking, 5ATM water resistance and 7 to 10 days between charges in normal use. Amazfit Band 7 goes further on endurance, averaging about 20 days per charge with sleep and heart rate tracking that testers found as reliable as bands costing several times more. For a first tracker, or for a parent who wants steps and sleep without a charging routine, these two are genuinely the right answer.

zh-tw.commentary:
2026 年的健身手環市場，真正決定你該買哪一台的關鍵已經從感測器規格轉移到商業模式了。一邊是買斷制，錢付一次就結束。另一邊是訂閱制，帳單每個月都會再來一次。所以我這份排名直接用三年總持有成本當主軸，把月費全部算進去之後，順序跟一般評測站的結論會有明顯落差。

Garmin Venu 4 拿第一。它的健康狀態監測會先摸清楚你自己的心率、HRV 跟體溫平常落在哪裡，其中一項開始偏離就主動提醒，這個價位帶第一次有手錶把警示的基準放在你本人身上。生活紀錄再把昨晚的咖啡因跟酒精連到當晚的睡眠分數，整個循環就閉起來了。續航 12 天，Garmin Connect 沒有任何功能被鎖在付費牆後面，台灣官方售價 NT$16,990，三年後你付的還是這一筆。

Garmin Venu 3 第二，NT$14,990，對大多數人來說它才是更划算的那一台。步數、心率、睡眠分期的日常準確度跟 Venu 4 同級，14 天續航，Body Battery 跟睡眠教練一樣包在硬體價裡。多出來的那兩千塊買的是健康狀態監測跟生活紀錄這兩層，你會真的去看那兩頁的話才值得。

Fitbit Charge 6 是我會推薦給大多數人的那一台，NT$5,190。睡眠趨勢報告的可讀性我用過最好，看完當下就知道明天該調整什麼，內建 ECG 心律偵測與 EDA 壓力感測，戴在手上輕到會忘記。

說真的，今年這個品類最有意思的產品是 Fitbit Air。Google 在 5 月 26 日推出，售價 99.99 美元，12 公克，一條錶帶加一顆小感測石，數據全部進 Google Health App，上面再疊一個 Gemini AI 健康教練。核心的睡眠、心率、步數終身免費。實測數據撐得住這個定價，兩週對比測試中它的總睡眠時間跟 Oura Ring 4 平均只差十三分鐘左右，靜止心率差約 3 bpm，2026 年 JMIR Formative Research 的研究更指出 Fitbit 在運動當下的光學心率準確度領先 Oura。台灣目前沒有引進，要買得走代購，這是唯一的門檻。

Oura Ring 5 六月四日開賣，399 美元，比 Ring 4 小了四成，是現在買得到最小的智慧戒指。讓 Ring 4 值得戴的睡眠與恢復評分完整保留下來，而這次的縮小就是我把它排在 Ring 4 前面的理由。台灣一樣沒有官方通路，要買得走代購。

坦白講，把三年帳算出來最有感。Fitbit Air 三年約 NT$3,140。WHOOP Peak 一年 239 美元，三年約 NT$22,400。Oura Ring 5 硬體加月費三年約 NT$19,600。這兩台各自有值得買的人，我在下面說清楚。

highlights.title: Garmin Venu 4 第一名，因為它的警示是對著你自己的基準線
highlights.body: 健康狀態監測是我把 Venu 4 放到 Venu 3 前面的關鍵。它會先摸清楚你的靜止心率、HRV 跟體溫平常落在哪裡，其中一項開始移動就跳提醒，等於在你自己有感覺之前，就先抓到那個快感冒的日子。生活紀錄接著告訴你咖啡因跟那杯酒對當晚睡眠做了什麼，警示就帶著原因一起出現。12 天續航的實際意義在於它會真的留在你手上過夜，而睡眠數據就是這樣累積出來的。這些功能全部含在 NT$16,990 裡面，沒有任何東西要續約。

highlights.title: Fitbit Air 是這個品類這幾年最重要的一次發表
highlights.body: Google 把螢幕整個拿掉，重量壓到 12 公克，定價 99.99 美元，睡眠、心率、步數、血氧與皮膚溫度終身免費。準確度站得住腳，兩週同時配戴的對比測試裡總睡眠時間跟 Oura Ring 4 平均差距約十三分鐘，靜止心率差約 3 bpm，2026 年 JMIR Formative Research 的研究則顯示 Fitbit 在運動狀態下的光學心率比 Oura 準。付一次錢、數據永遠是你的，這在整份榜單裡是最強的價值主張。台灣讀者要走代購，換算約三千出頭，這個價位在台灣大概是一頓好一點的聚餐加一件外套，門檻不高。

highlights.title: 比規格之前先把訂閱費算進去，順序會整個換掉
highlights.body: 三年總帳是這樣：Fitbit Air 約 NT$3,140，Fitbit Charge 6 NT$5,190，Amazfit Active 2 NT$3,599，Garmin Venu 3 NT$14,990。訂閱陣營這邊，Oura Ring 4 硬體加每月 5.99 美元月費，三年約 NT$17,600，WHOOP Peak 一年 239 美元，三年約 NT$22,400，會員費本身含硬體與 PowerPack 充電器。願意把恢復追蹤當成長期服務來訂的人，後面兩台合理。想要買完就結束的人，買斷陣營才是你該逛的那一區。

highlights.title: 準確度要分軸看，貴的那台只贏在它自己的那一軸
highlights.body: 2026 年這一輪實測最有價值的結論是，這些裝置各自擅長不同的東西。Oura Ring 4 在睡眠分期與夜間 HRV 領先，總睡眠時間偏差只有約三分鐘，是這群裡最小的。WHOOP 5.0 在高強度訓練週期的連續負荷與恢復監測領先。Fitbit 拿下運動當下的光學心率。Garmin 拿下步數、運動與睡眠的全面一致性。先確定自己最在意哪一軸，價格的問題大概就自己有答案了。

highlights.title: 兩千元以下，小米手環 10 跟 Amazfit Band 7 給的東西遠超過價格
highlights.body: 小米手環 10 台灣官方售價 NT$1,199，這代螢幕放大到 1.72 吋 AMOLED，步數與心率準確，5ATM 防水，正常使用七到十天充一次電，這個價格在台灣大概就是兩張電影票。Amazfit Band 7 續航更誇張，平均二十天充一次，睡眠與心率的可靠度被實測認為跟貴好幾倍的手環同級。第一支手環，或是想幫家裡長輩買一支記步數跟睡眠、又不想每兩天提醒他充電的，這兩支就是正解。

references.title: Garmin's rumored screen-less wearable just might be the subscription-free Whoop rival I've been waiting for
Google is preparing to take on Whoop with a screen-free Fitbit
Best fitness trackers 2026: Apple Watch, Fitbit, Samsung and more

en.commentary: The most interesting thing happening in this category right now is a fight over the subscription, and it is worth understanding before you buy anything. Whoop built the screenless band business on a model where the hardware is nearly free and the monthly fee never stops. Google answered with the Fitbit Air, which is already fourth on this board at 8.9, and Garmin is reportedly preparing a screenless tracker of its own, currently referred to as the Cirqa, with the explicit pitch being no subscription at all. If Garmin ships that, it lands directly on top of Whoop 5, which sits eighth at 8.3 largely because the recurring cost drags its total cost score down. I am not ranking a rumour, so nothing moves today, but anyone considering a Whoop membership this month should know a subscription-free alternative from a company with genuine sensor credibility is plausibly weeks away. Garmin Venu 4 holds first at 9.5 and my reasoning has not changed. It is the only device here that gives you a full week of battery, an AMOLED display you can read in Taipei summer sun, and no ongoing fee for the metrics that matter. Total cost of ownership over three years is the number most buyers skip, and Venu 4 wins it against every subscription device on this list. Fitbit Charge 6 holds third at 9.1 as the cheapest band with genuinely trustworthy heart rate during steady state cardio. Samsung's Galaxy Watch 9 began shipping August 7 on the Snapdragon Wear Elite chipset, and I am testing it now for a future entry. No rank or score changes today.

highlights.title: Garmin's rumoured Cirqa is aimed straight at the Whoop subscription
highlights.body: Reports point to a screenless Garmin tracker pitched explicitly without a monthly fee. Whoop 5 sits eighth at 8.3 on this board mainly because recurring cost pulls down its total cost score. A subscription-free band from a company with Garmin's sensor track record would change the value calculation for that entire segment, which is why I would wait before signing a new Whoop year.

highlights.title: Three year cost of ownership is the number that decides this category
highlights.body: Venu 4 holds first at 9.5 because the purchase price is the entire price. A subscription tracker at a modest monthly fee costs more than a flagship Garmin by month thirty, and the data it returns is not thirty percent better. Work out the three year total before comparing feature lists, because that single calculation reorders most of this board.

highlights.title: The Charge 6 is the cheapest band whose heart rate I actually trust
highlights.body: Optical heart rate on inexpensive bands falls apart during interval work, but the Charge 6 tracks steady state cardio closely enough to train from. For someone running a fixed route three times a week and wanting an honest trend line, that accuracy at this price is the whole recommendation, and it keeps third at 9.1.

highlights.title: Sunlight legibility matters more in Taiwan than any sensor spec
highlights.body: A tracker you cannot read at noon on a bike path in Kaohsiung is a tracker you check later on a phone, which defeats the point of wearing it. Venu 4's AMOLED at full brightness stays legible in direct summer sun, and that practical detail affects daily use more than a marginal difference in heart rate sampling.

zh-tw.commentary:
這個品類現在最有看頭的是一場關於訂閱費的戰爭，買之前真的該先搞懂。

Whoop 靠的商業模式是硬體幾乎免費、月費永遠不停。Google 用 Fitbit Air 回應，那台已經在榜上第四名 8.9。而根據報導，Garmin 也在準備自家的無螢幕手環，代號 Cirqa，主打的賣點就是完全免訂閱。如果 Garmin 真的推出來，那會直接壓在 Whoop 5 頭上，後者目前第八名 8.3，很大一部分就是被持續性費用把總成本分數拖下來的。

我不會照傳言排名，所以今天不動。不過這個月正在考慮辦 Whoop 會員的人，該知道一個有真材實料感測器技術的品牌，很可能在幾週內端出免訂閱的替代方案。

Garmin Venu 4 續坐第一 9.5，理由沒變。它是榜上唯一同時給你一週續航、台北夏天太陽底下看得清楚的 AMOLED、而且重要數據不用另外付錢的裝置。三年持有總成本是多數買家會跳過的數字，而 Venu 4 對上榜單裡任何一台訂閱制裝置都贏。

Fitbit Charge 6 第三名 9.1，是穩態有氧心率真的可信的最便宜手環。Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 已於 8 月 7 日出貨，搭 Snapdragon Wear Elite，我正在測，之後會考慮進榜。今天名次分數不動。

highlights.title: Garmin 傳聞中的 Cirqa 是直接衝著 Whoop 訂閱費來的
highlights.body: 多方報導指向一款無螢幕的 Garmin 手環，主打就是不收月費。Whoop 5 在榜上第八名 8.3，主要就是被持續性費用把總成本分數拉下來。一個由 Garmin 這種感測器實績的品牌推出的免訂閱手環，會改寫整個級距的價值算式，所以現在要續約 Whoop 年費的人，我建議先等一下。

highlights.title: 決定這個品類勝負的數字是三年持有成本
highlights.body: Venu 4 拿第一 9.5，因為買斷價就是全部的價格。一台月費不算貴的訂閱手環，到第三十個月的總花費就超過旗艦 Garmin，而它給的數據並沒有好上三成。比較功能表之前先算三年總價，光這一個計算就會讓榜單重排。

highlights.title: Charge 6 是心率我真的信得過的最便宜手環
highlights.body: 便宜手環的光學心率遇到間歇訓練就會崩掉，但 Charge 6 在穩態有氧的追蹤精度足以拿來當訓練依據。對一週跑三次固定路線、只想要一條誠實趨勢線的人來說，這個價位有這個準度就是全部的推薦理由，第三名 9.1 站得住。

highlights.title: 在台灣，太陽下看不看得清楚比感測器規格更重要

highlights.body: Garmin 不對感測器收集到的數據另外收費，而好幾家競爭對手把分析鎖在月費後面。在一台裝置的使用年限內，這個差額超過機器本身的售價，第一名就是這樣來的。

highlights.title: 上一代才是 CP 值答案
highlights.body: Venu 3 的日常表現跟新款幾乎一樣，現在還有折扣。在一個好的生態系裡買前一代，一直都是這個品類最會花錢的做法。

highlights.title: Fitbit 是在解釋，不只是回報
highlights.body: Charge 6 的 App 把讀值翻譯成白話建議，不留給你自己解讀。想改善習慣而不是想研究圖表的人，這個呈現方式的價值超過感測器精度。

highlights.title: 把五年訂閱費算出來
highlights.body: 只比售價會蓋掉需要月費的裝置的真實成本。加上五年訂閱之後，這份榜單的順序會大幅改變，誰真的比較便宜也會不一樣。

en.commentary:
The Garmin Venu 4 holds first at 9.5 because it wins the two factors that actually determine whether a tracker stays on your wrist after month three. Accuracy at 9.6 means the heart rate and sleep data are worth acting on, and battery life at 9.4 means you are not choosing between wearing it overnight and having it charged for tomorrow's run. Garmin held a launch event on 25 August, so watch that line for movement over the next few weeks.

The more interesting development this month sits outside the current board. The Fitbit co-founders launched Luffu, a screen free wrist wearable designed for continuous monitoring of ageing family members, with a jewellery style design rather than a medical one. That is a real product category forming, and it points at where passive health tracking goes next. Google shipped the Pixel Watch 5 on 12 August with cloud based GPS post processing that the company claims doubles route accuracy in difficult environments.

On the board itself, the Fitbit Charge 6 at 9.1 remains my recommendation for most people. It costs a fraction of a full smartwatch, the app is the friendliest here at 9.4, and the three year total cost score of 9.3 reflects that nothing important sits behind a subscription. The Fitbit Air at 8.9 is the cheapest honest entry point.

On rings, the Oura Ring 5 at 8.6 gives the best sleep data on this list, and that 6.2 total cost score is the membership fee doing its work. Ask yourself whether you will still open the app daily in year two. If yes, the ring is worth it. If you are unsure, start with a Charge 6.

highlights.title: Accuracy plus battery keeps it on your wrist
highlights.body: The Venu 4 scores 9.6 and 9.4 on those two factors, which is why it stays first. Data worth acting on and no nightly charging decision is what survives past month three.

highlights.title: A new passive monitoring category is forming
highlights.body: The Fitbit co-founders launched Luffu on 25 August, a screen free wrist wearable for continuously monitoring ageing relatives with a jewellery style design. That points at where this market goes next.

highlights.title: Charge 6 is the right answer for most people
highlights.body: A 9.4 app score, a 9.3 three year cost score and nothing important locked behind a subscription. It does the job a full smartwatch does for a fraction of the money.

highlights.title: Rings earn their price through year two
highlights.body: The Oura Ring 5 delivers the best sleep data here, and its 6.2 cost score is the membership. The honest test is whether you will still open the app daily twelve months in.

zh-tw.commentary:
Garmin Venu 4 守住第一 9.5，贏在兩個真正決定「第三個月後你還戴不戴」的項目。準確度 9.6 代表心率跟睡眠資料可以拿來調作息，續航 9.4 代表你不用在戴著睡覺跟明天有電之間二選一。Garmin 八月二十五日辦了發表活動，這一列接下來值得盯。

這個月更有意思的發展在榜外。Fitbit 共同創辦人推出 Luffu，一款無螢幕腕戴裝置，主打持續照看家中長輩，外型走首飾路線。Google 則在八月十二日推出 Pixel Watch 5，主打雲端 GPS 後處理，官方說複雜環境下路徑準確度提升一倍。

回到榜上，Fitbit Charge 6 9.1 依然是我給多數人的答案。App 體驗 9.4 是這裡最親切的，三年總成本 9.3 反映重要功能都沒鎖在訂閱後面。

戒指這邊，Oura Ring 5 8.6 的睡眠資料最好，6.2 的成本分數就是會員費在說話。第二年你還會每天開 App 嗎，會的話它值得。

highlights.title: 準確度加續航才留得住你的手腕
highlights.body: Venu 4 在這兩項拿到 9.6 跟 9.4，這就是它守住第一的原因。資料可以拿來行動，晚上又不用做取捨，才撐得過第三個月。

highlights.title: 被動監測正在長成一個新品類
highlights.body: Fitbit 共同創辦人八月二十五日推出 Luffu，無螢幕腕戴、首飾外型，專門持續照看家中長輩。這指出這個市場接下來的方向。

highlights.title: 多數人的正解還是 Charge 6
highlights.body: App 體驗 9.4、三年成本 9.3，重要功能都沒鎖在訂閱後面。花全功能智慧錶的零頭，做的是同一件事。

highlights.title: 戒指要撐到第二年才值回票價
highlights.body: Oura Ring 5 的睡眠資料是這裡最好的，6.2 的成本分數就是會員費。誠實的檢驗方式是：一年後你還會每天開 App 嗎。
